title: rollout-incident-synthesis-safety-gates-and-automated-circuit-breakers
creator: Asha Patel
description: Synthesize learnings from the recent failed model deployment that triggered an automated fallback. The goal is to produce a compact incident synthesis, formalize additional safety gates (pre-rollout and in-flight), and implement automated circuit-breakers that stop rollouts when divergence or KPI degradation crosses adaptive thresholds. This ticket consolidates runbook updates, telemetry thresholds, and follow-ups for A/B analysis, shadow traffic scoring, and a small control-plane automation prototype.
steps_taken: 1) Immediately halted the active rollout and reverted to previous model variant via the control plane rollback API (commit: github.com/redwood-inference/pr/4287). 2) Routed 100% of production traffic away from affected nodes while preserving read-only diagnostics. 3) Enabled extended tracing for the last 6 hours of requests and persisted KV cache snapshots for analysis. 4) Notified impacted customer success teams and opened a status page entry. 5) Ran scheduled synthetic validation suite that reproduces the divergence patterns under the same load profile.
findings:
- Root cause appears to be a rare interaction between an LLM context-serialization change and the runtime's KV cache eviction heuristics under bursty prefix distributions. The change led to stale KV segments for ~0.4% of requests, magnifying prediction drift for low-frequency long-context flows.
- Canary metrics (latency and simple top-1 mismatch) did not trigger because the divergence signal was mostly semantic and surfaced in downstream reranking F1 and customer-facing hallucination counts, which are not part of our default canary scoreset.
- Shadow traffic capture was incomplete: only 70% of shadowed requests contained the full user metadata needed to evaluate downstream metrics.
- Automatic rollback fired, but the circuit threshold was static and tuned conservatively; it reacted after 18 minutes of degraded quality. There is room to make thresholds adaptive and to add fast-stop heuristics for semantic quality regressions.
- Observability gaps: no single composite score for semantic regressions, and delayed aggregation for reranker metrics (6-10 minute windows) slowed decision-making.
